workload.description: Three groups of deterministic payloads, 3 MiB per group, separated by 12 seconds; each record put individually at least 1 second apart; 25 second additional idle before waiting for minute +5 second subscription start. One natural 5-minute subscription, no deliberate client disconnect.
workload.payloadRule: ASCII label group-index followed by newline, repeated and truncated to specified bytes; SHA256 and byte count replace binary Data in captured inputs/outputs.

metricWindow.note: Fixed whole-minute window; includes before activity and two complete minutes after subscription. Later polling does not change query window. Service aggregation minute may differ from client arrival minute. Natural stream termination avoids deliberate partial consumption but cannot prove no unobserved service-side publication.

derivedAnalysis.classification: Derived calculations and bounded interpretation only; native SDK responses and event frames remain in calls without invented expected values.

positiveBacklogInterpretation.conclusion: Native positive lag is not the timestamp distance between last written and last returned records. Its value is consistent with age of the last returned record at service publication time. Caught-up lag is zero despite old records.
positiveBacklogInterpretation.remainingUncertainty: Only one positive frame observed. Exact server sampling instant, rounding/quantization, and general backlog formula are not established; decoded frame arrival occurs after transfer of a 7.5 MiB payload and is not server publication time. Do not turn the approximate age consistency into an exact native formula.

observations: Positive-backlog minute 11:29 UTC has 12 frame samples: two nonempty frames and ten empty frames. Native backlog Sum/Maximum 88000, Minimum 0, Average 7333.333333333333.

Consumer event Bytes and enhanced-shard OutgoingBytes distributions are identical, with SampleCount 12, Sum 9437238, Minimum 0, Maximum 7864368, Average 786436.5 in the positive minute. Values equal payload bytes plus UTF-8 partition-key bytes, grouped per frame rather than per record.
Consumer event Records and enhanced-shard OutgoingRecords distributions are identical, with SampleCount 12, Sum 18, Minimum 0, Maximum 16, Average 1.5 in the positive minute.
Four wholly subscribed idle minutes 11:30 through 11:33 UTC each have 12 zero-valued backlog/bytes/records frame samples and 12 success-one samples.

Terminal partial minute 11:34 UTC has one decoded empty frame and one backlog/bytes/records sample, but native Event.Success has SampleCount 2, Sum 1, Minimum 0, Maximum 1, Average 0.5. Clean SDK event-stream EOF does not explain the native zero-success sample.
SubscribeToShard.Success has exactly one sample of value one in the admission minute.
nativeMetricCorrelation.disconnectAndPartialMinuteAmbiguity: No deliberate client disconnect, reconnect, or admission retry occurred. Native iterator exhaustion was observed after about five minutes. First/last subscription minutes are partial. CloudWatch samples describe service publication, not guaranteed client-delivered frame count, and no cause is assigned to the terminal zero-success sample.

queryWindow.note: Fixed whole-minute window; includes before activity and two complete minutes after subscription. Later polling does not change query window. Service aggregation minute may differ from client arrival minute. Natural stream termination avoids deliberate partial consumption but cannot prove no unobserved service-side publication.

boundedMetricAbsences.meaning: No datapoints returned for these dimension/metric/minute combinations by the final recheck; absence is bounded to this observed window, not an assertion about all idle streams or future publications.

observationMethod.frameArrivalMeaning: Host timestamp immediately after boto3 yields each completely decoded event, before payload digest serialization; not a server publication timestamp.
observationMethod.binaryPayloadHandling: SDK native metadata retained; Data replaced by explicit byteLength and SHA256 descriptor. Inputs regenerate exactly from workload payloadRule and labels.

documentationContext.relevantDefinition: SubscribeToShardEvent.Bytes and Records are single-event distributions; enhanced OutgoingBytes/OutgoingRecords include SubscribeToShard events; event Success is emitted every time an event is published successfully.
A successful subscription receives events for up to five minutes and must be renewed explicitly.
MillisBehindLatest indicates how far behind current time the consumer is, with zero indicating caught-up; ContinuationSequenceNumber tracks progress even without new records.
GetMetricStatistics supports five summary statistics, aggregates by the requested period, does not guarantee output order, and has inclusive start/exclusive end boundaries.
